messages:
maria: Hey folks — hitting a weird duplicate-job issue in the onboarding sample app (JS SDK). Sequence: token rotate -> backend returns early ack, then 429 on subsequent call, client retry creates a second job. Minimal repro attached. Anyone seen this?

ajay: Can you paste the SDK retry/backoff config you're using? Is an idempotency key being set/persisted?

maria: config is basically default from the quickstart:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, maxRetries: 3, backoff: { baseMs: 200, maxMs: 2000, jitter: true } });
await client.createJob(payload); // sampleapp doesn't generate an idempotency key anywhere
```

noah: SDK should generate an idempotency header for non-streaming RPCs by default. Which SDK version?

maria: 2.1.0 (installed via quickstart). Repro notes: start sample app, trigger token refresh (rotate key on auth server), then immediately post job. The auth rotation causes one request to early-ack (server sends ack before DB write), the next call hits 429 quota while our client retries and resends the same semantic action without a stable idempotency key -> duplicate effective job.

ajay: Sounds like a race where the generated idempotency key lives only in-memory per-request and gets lost across token refresh/retry path. Two quick ideas:
- persist the idempotency key into the request context before any network call so retries reuse it
- add jittered exponential backoff with randomized seed per request so retries don't line up

Sketch patch:```js
function sendWithIdempotency(req) {
  req.headers['Idempotency-Key'] = req.headers['Idempotency-Key'] || generateIdempotencyKey();
  persistInLocalStore(req.id, req.headers['Idempotency-Key']); // survives token refresh hooks
  return retry(() => http.send(req), { retries: 3, backoff: exponentialWithJitter });
}
```

noah: For streaming/long-poll endpoints adding a stable header is trickier, but for create/update RPCs this should be safe. Also server-side dedupe according to that header would help (server can ignore duplicate non-idempotent side effects if same key seen).

maria: I can open a PR to the JS SDK to: 1) persist generated idempotency keys in the request context across auth hooks, 2) ensure jittered backoff is the default for 429s, and 3) add a sampleapp test harness that flips the token and asserts no duplicate side-effects. Assigning review to @ajay. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI: flaky-replay-test timed out on node12 matrix, failing on the new persistence test (timeout 30s).

maria: Thanks — I'll look at test timeout. Might need to mock the rotate/ack sequence more aggressively in the harness to make it deterministic.

ajay: Also suggest adding a lightweight telemetry event when a retry uses a persisted idempotency key so we can monitor frequency in prod.

maria: Good call, will add metric. I'll open the PR and link here.

maria: TL;DR: root cause = in-memory idempotency generation + token-rotation race + 429 retry sending side-effect twice; plan = persist idempotency, default jittered backoff for 429, server-side dedupe guidance, sampleapp harness + telemetry.
